image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Single massive round concrete pier column for an elevated expressway, tall cylindrical shaft on a low square footing, flaring at the top into a wide flat hammerhead cap beam with tapered underside and chamfered edges, small rectangular bearing pads on the cap top Materials: Pale grey cast concrete with form-tie holes in a grid, dark water streaks under the cap, black diesel soot on the lower shaft, patched spalls, faded painted chevron band near the base.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 280/16,000 triangles, 4/12 draw calls, 4/8 materials, 4/16 unique geometries, three canvases.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 12.5 x 12.0 x 4.4 off the built module (bounds +-6.25, 0..12, +-2.2). Cap taper from the column head at 9.15 to 1.2 m ends, chamfered top arrises, 2.8 m column, 4.4 m footing; proxy band table mean |delta w| 0.122 with the residual entirely in the contract's wider cap (bands 8-9: 1.02 vs 0.73 H) and the column bands 0.23 vs 0.27 H.

Two 0.70 x 0.50 pads proud of the cap top by 0.15 m with their tops at exactly 12.00; 80 mm chamfers on both top arrises read as a highlight line at az 000 and the hero; the cap's tie grid and water streaks show at every azimuth.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's cap has a lightly chamfered long underside edge that is not built.

featureReviews.evidence: Probed on beauty-000: shaft 154 (plate 153), cap side 164 (164), cap top 197 (193), soot 102-126 (plate 68, held up for the gate). Tie grid at 0.67 m, lift joints at 1.5 m and 90 cloud patches give the shaft a rendered spread the first flat build lacked; soot occupies the lower 40% of the shaft with 70 blots.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's soot sits mainly on one flank; the canvas wraps it.

featureReviews.evidence: 16 red-and-white diagonal stripe pairs round the foot, 0.7 m tall from 0.75 to 1.45, on a shell 5 mm proud of the column; visible at all four azimuths.

name: Expressway Hammerhead Pier
nameTh: เสาตอม่อทางด่วนหัวค้อน
notes: The classic Bangkok expressway pier (Sirat / Chalerm Maha Nakhon). MODULAR CONTRACT for the highway set: ground at y=0, the cap's bearing seat at y=12.00 (the tops of two 0.70 x 0.50 pads standing 0.15 above the cap top at 11.85) so a deck module placed with its pivot at y=12 sits on it; cap 12.5 m wide along X to match the 12.5 m deck width and 2.6 m deep along Z so two 16 m deck modules meeting over it butt at z=+-8 without touching the cap faces. BUILT (2026-09-10): column 2.8 m diameter, footing 4.4 x 4.4 x 0.6 m -- the notes said 2.4 / 3.5 and the Meshy proxy read the column at 0.27 H (3.25 m) and the footing at 0.43 H (5.2 m); 2.8 / 4.4 splits the difference so the pier reads as the plate does under a cap the contract makes wider. Declared depth corrected 2.6 -> 4.4, the footing, which is what the bounding box is; the cap stays 2.6. No interior, no rebar.
